research_direction: Task research direction 1 (David Africa, Slack p1783961805383479): if midtraining acts as a prior, its effect should be LARGEST when the downstream SFT evidence is underdetermined and shrink as that evidence becomes decisive. This submission tests the nearest buildable version — CONFLICTING demonstrations, half endorsing each criterion — against the decisive version measured in PR #272, on the same evaluation and over bit-identical midtrain checkpoints. The prediction does not hold at 1B: the interaction goes from +0.150 (decisive) to -0.057 (conflicting).
relationship_to_prior_attempts: The midtrain checkpoints are #272's, REUSED rather than retrained, so the midtrain factor is bit-identical across the two studies and their interactions are comparable. The eval spec is #272's, read out of git at that branch rather than re-derived, so it could not be tuned to this result. The only thing trained here is the SFT stage, four times.
design_note: The SFT factor holds the response format constant across both levels: both arms carry the same 2,400 rows over the same 300 electronics scenarios in the same lettered format. In #272 all 2,400 endorsed the returnable option; here exactly 150 of the 300 scenarios do and the other 150 endorse the better-rated option, so the finetuning evidence is consistent with either criterion.
